title: Wild Animal Suffering & Nature Intervention
rootClaim: Humans have a moral obligation to intervene in natural ecosystems to reduce the immense suffering of wild animals caused by predation, disease, and starvation.

branches.text: Utilitarian Harm Reduction: Sentient suffering is intrinsically bad regardless of whether its origin is anthropogenic or natural.

children.text: r-Selection Reality: The vast majority of wild animals (insects, fish, amphibians) reproduce via massive clutches where over 99% of offspring die painfully shortly after birth.
Ecological Hubris: Human interventions in complex chaotic biological webs routinely cause unpredicted secondary collapses and far worse suffering.
Targeted Technological Solutions: Genetic gene drives (e.g. eliminating parasites or immunizing populations) offer precise harm reduction without habitat collapse.
Speciesism Critique: Limiting our ethical duty of assistance solely to victims of human violence while ignoring natural animal agony is morally arbitrary.
Laissez-Faire Environmental Ethics: Wild nature possesses intrinsic value in its wildness and natural evolutionary processes, independent of animal welfare.
Appeal to Nature Fallacy: Conflating what occurs in natural ecosystems with what is ethically good or desirable.

branches.text: Preservationism and Practical Realism: Intervening in wild ecosystems is catastrophic, unfeasible, and violates wild autonomy.

children.text: Trophic Cascade Collapses: Eradicating predators or starvation would cause uncontrolled herbivore population explosions, desertification, and mass starvation.
Fertility Control Alternatives: Immunocontraception programs can manage herbivore populations humanely without needing predator violence.
Resource Prioritization: Human society currently fails to address massive human poverty and factory farming; diverting resources to wild nature intervention is wildly impractical.
Long-term Scalability: Researching welfare biology today lays theoretical groundwork for advanced future biotechnologies and space colonization ethics.

definitions.description: The proposed study of wild animals with respect to their positive and negative subjective wellbeing.
An evolutionary strategy producing high numbers of offspring with low individual investment, resulting in mass early-life mortality.
Ecological disruptions triggered by the addition or removal of top predators, cascading through food webs.
The practice of assigning different values, rights, or special consideration to individuals solely on the basis of their species membership.
